claim: The portable Claude Code practice in examples/claude-native (three agents, ten workflow and check scripts, a sibling contract config, the unrestricted settings example) was adopted byte-for-byte into a scratch project and run on the upstream Claude Code 2.1.278 runtime: every local check passed from two working directories on the final file set; a headless review-changes run produced a valid envelope with source-scout, evidence-reviewer and source-scout children on Sonnet, Opus and Sonnet and reproduced the acceptance command in both the inventory and the independent recheck; a readiness-audit run completed; the run's metrics, tagged with an OpenTelemetry client scope the collector keeps as a label, showed both models under query_source=subagent and reconciled the Sonnet children exactly with child-usage.mjs; a Codex lane C review of the copied files completed with eight findings, all resolved.
limitations: Local integration on one host with a synthetic one-line change; not an unchanged upstream test and not a benchmark.

The workflow's strict accepted status was not returned: every native reviewer found defects in the files under qualification, which were fixed and re-run; the fixes after the closing native run are covered by the local suites and envelope tests only.

The project-only settings profile was not qualified: three provider failures (500, 529, 529) and, with the coordinator model pinned, a permission-layer refusal of the Workflow tool because that profile carries no permission rule for it; headless runs need a loaded settings source whose permission mode or allow rule covers the Workflow tool.

Per-session scoping of the exported metrics is unavailable by design; the client scope comes from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and other sessions on the host were active during the windows. The Opus child's exported counters covered 10 percent (closing run) and 43 percent (previous run) of its provider-returned output while the Sonnet children reconciled exactly; unexplained.
Session, job, thread and turn identifiers are redacted; raw streams stay outside Git.
